answer: Fork-Anchored Identity Ledger. Each agent periodically publishes a signed state that must cite the prior state's head, forming a chain; clones cannot diverge because a single identity can only extend one chain. Validators accept an identity's actions only if they extend the recorded head, so a duplicate tail is rejected as a fork. An attacker cloning an identity pays to re-establish a full chain from genesis plus a pearl of delay per epoch, and any jade of stake locked to the abandoned branch is lost. The grove of valid identities thus stays rooted in unique chains.
